title: Finite-projective summand equations
statement:
For a finite projective $F^r$ and a displayed splitting $(i_r,p_r)$, the
arrows $\pi_{h,E,F^r}$ and $\rho_{F^r}$ are inverse and are independent of
the chosen finite-free summand presentation.

proof.text: Apply coefficient naturality to the inclusion and projection of the displayed degree-zero splitting. Construct the finite-free single-complex package with identity inclusion and projection in degree zero and zero maps in all other degrees. The singleObjXSelf isomorphism transports the original degree-zero package maps to actual maps M to the finite free sheaf and back; their composite is identity.

The single-complex functor, Q, LF, TR, TS and RF preserve the two splitting composites. Apply the finite-free inverse theorem at rank P.N(0) and shift zero. The two naturality squares for each splitting map transport both inverse equations down the retract; the private inverse_pair_of_retract lemma spells out the two associative computations.

Apply coefficient naturality to the identity cochain map, using P for the source package and P-prime for the target package. Both functors map identity to identity. The two naturality squares therefore give equality of the forward arrows and equality of the reverse arrows. Product extensionality gives equality of pairs without unfolding their representative constructions.
